questions.question: The National Rail Plan announced in the Union Budget of 2021-22 aims to create a future ready railway system by which of the following years?

__
 
• During the union budget, 2021- 2022 the Finance Minister announces that Indian Railways have prepared a **national rail plan for India 2030**.
 
• The plan is to create a ‘future-ready’ railway system by 2030.
 
• The main aim of the national rail plan is to bring down the logistics cost.
 
• It is expected that Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (DFC) and Eastern DFC will be commissioned by June 2022.
 
• It also announces the 100% electrification of broad gauge rail tracks by December 2023. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Introduction of aesthetically designed Vista Dome LHB coach on tourist routes.

• The budget also provided a record sum of Rs. 1,10,055 crore for Railways of which Rs. 1,07,100 crore is for capital expenditure.

questions.question: A celt is ______ from the Neolithic period.

__
 
• **A celt is a tool from the Neolithic period.**
 
• The tools and weapons of the Neolithic Age were better and sharper than the Paleolithic Age.
 
• **A polished stone called a celt** was **used to make tools.**
 
• Some newly developed **tools like sickles, bows, arrows and improved axes were made in the Neolithic Age.​**

• ​In India, the period occurs between** 7,000 B.C. to 1,000 B.C.**
 
• **Development of settled agriculture **and the use of **tools and weapons made of polished stones.**
 
• The **major crops** grown during this period were **ragi, horse gram, cotton, rice, wheat, and barley.**
 
• One of the remarkable achievements of the Neolithic Period was the** invention of the wheel.**
 
• It brought **rapid progress in man's life.**
 
• The wheel was used in horse carts and bullock carts that helped man a lot to carry heavy loads.
 
• Therefore, in this period** transport became quite easy and quick.**
 
• The **wheel **was also used for **spinning and weaving.**
 
• It also helped in **pottery.**
 
• **Man-made beautiful pots** to keep **food grains and store water.**

questions.question: Koteshwar Hydroelectric Power Project is located on the river ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhagirathi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Koteshwar Dam__

 __
 
• It is a gravity dam on the Bhagirathi River, located 22 km from the Tehri Dam in Tehri District, Uttarakhand.
 
• The dam is part of the Tehri Hydropower Complex and serves to regulate the Tehri Dam's tailrace for irrigation and create the lower reservoir of the Tehri Pumped Storage Power Station.
 
 
 
• Bhagirathi__​
 __
 
• The Bhagirathi river is a Himalayan river that flows in Uttarakhand State.
 
• It is one of the two headstreams of the pious Ganga river.
 
• It originates from Gaumukh Glacier and flows about 193 km before merging with Alaknanda to form River Ganga at Devprayag.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gomati**__

 __
 
• The Gomti river is a Monsoon and Groundwater fed river.
 
• That originated from Gomat Taal (earlier known as Fulhaar jheel) near Madho Tanda, Pilibhit district of Uttar Pradesh state.
 
• It is a tributary of the Ganges river. 
 
• Its length extends 960 km through Uttar Pradesh and meets the Ganges river near Saidpur, and Kaithi 27 km from Varanasi district of Uttar Pradesh state.
 
 
 
• ​**Koshi**__
 __
 
• The Kosi is a 720 km long transboundary river which flows through Nepal, Tibet and India. 
 
• It drains the northern slopes of Tibet and the southern slopes of Nepal.
 
• It is also known as Saptakoshi due to its seven upper tributaries, namely, the **Indrawati, the Sun Koshi, the Tama Koshi, the Likhu, the Dudh Koshi, the Arun and the Tamor**. 
 
 
 
• **Damodar**__
 
• The source of the Damodar river is Chota Nagpur Plateau (Palamau hills in Jharkhand) and the mouth is Hooghly River, Rupnarayan River.
 
• The river bifurcates into two channels at Beguahana.
 
 
• The main flow passes through the Mundeswari channel and discharges into Rupnarayan.
 
• The other one Amta channel carries discharge during high floods and outfalls into the Hooghly.
 
 
 
• **The Damodar River in India has four main dams:**

 Tilaiya: Located on the Barakar River

 Maithon: Located on the Barakar River

 Panchet: Located on the Damodar River

 Konar: Located on the Konar River

questions.question: Which of the following Amendment Acts of the Constitution of India abolished the privy purses and privileges of former rulers of princely states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer __**26th Amendment Act 1971**__**.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• Privy purses conferred ‘special status’ to the ruling class, which continued the British practice of ruler and ruled.
 
• ‘Privy purse’ was an added economic pressure on a newly born independent nation, that was ridden with poverty, hunger and security challenges.
 
• Therefore, the then Prime Minister, Indira Gandhi, argued the case for the abolition of the privy purse. So, by the 26th Amendment to the Constitution of India in 1971, ‘privy purse’ was abolished. The amendment leads to the omission of Articles 291 and 362.
 
• The payments of ‘privy purse’ were made to the former rulers under the constitutional provisions of Article 291 and Article 362.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Article 291 dealt with Privy purse sums of Rulers and was repealed by the Constitution in (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971.
 
• Article 362 dealt with the Rights and privileges of Rulers of Indian States and was repealed by the Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT belong to ‘Kingdom Fungi’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Euglena__.**

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Euglena belongs to the kingdom Protista.**
 
• Euglena is a single-celled organism with a well-defined nucleus.
 
• It** uses flagella for locomotion, **all these characteristics are **similar to the organisms belonging to the kingdom Protista.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• The living organism is placed into **five different kingdoms**:

 
 
• **Monera**

 
 
• **Prokaryotic organisms **are placed.
 
• They are a primitive type of organism some are fed on the host cell some **show symbiotic relations.**
 
• They are called prokaryotes because their **nucleus is present in cell cytoplasm without a nuclear membrane.**
 
 
 
• **Protista**
 
 
• This kingdom acts as a** connecting link between kingdom prokaryotes**.
 
• **Mostly aquatic and found in seas, freshwater, and moist soil. **
 
 
 
• **Fungi**
 
 
• Kingdom consists of species that are **heterotrophic, spore-forming, non-vascular, **achlorophyllous, and **eukaryotic organisms.**
 
• Their cell wall is made up of chitin or fungal cellulose and glycogen is a reserve food material.
 
• The study of fungi is called mycology.
 
• **Examples: Aspergillus, Mucor, Rhizopus.**
 
 
 
• **Plants**
 
 
• It is the **eukaryotic multicellular living organism** that shows the photosynthetic process.
 
• Acts as the** producer in the ecosystem**
 
• Their body is divided into roots, shoots, and leaves.
 
• They are divided into** crypto gramme (flower and seed-bearing plants) and phanerogamme (a plant with seeds and sex organs visible).**
 
 
 
• **Animalia**
 
 
• Kingdom** Animalia constitutes all animals.**
 
• Amongst the five kingdoms, the **largest kingdom is the animal kingdom.**
 
• Animals are **multicellular eukaryotes.**
 
• However, like plants, they do not possess chlorophyll or a cell wall.

questions.question: In order to prevent tooth decay safely and effectively by making use of water, it is subject to which of the following processes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __Fluoridation__.**

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Water fluoridation**** is the process of adjusting the amount of fluoride in drinking water to a level recommended for preventing tooth decay.**
 
• **Fluoride** has been **proven to protect teeth from decay.**
 
• **Bacteria in the mouth produce acid **when a person eats sugary foods.
 
• This** acid eats away minerals** from the tooth’s surface, **making the tooth weaker and increasing the chance of developing cavities.**
 
• **Fluoride helps to rebuild and strengthen the tooth’s surface, or enamel.**
 
• Water fluoridation prevents tooth decay by providing frequent and consistent contact with low levels of fluoride.
 
• Fluoride stops cavities from forming and can even rebuild the tooth’s surface.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• **Iodisation**

 
 
• ​Salt iodization has been the** preferred strategy to control and eliminate iodine deficiency disorders (IDD). **
 
• The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends that the** salt must have an iodine content of 15 parts per million (ppm) or more.**
 
 
 
• **Chlorination​**
 
 
• ​Chlorination is the process of **adding chlorine to drinking water to kill parasites, bacteria, and viruses.**
 
• **Chlorine levels up to 4 milligrams per liter **(mg/L or 4 parts per million (ppm)) are considered **safe in drinking water.**
 
 
 
• **Carbonization ****​**
 
 
• ​Carbonization is the **conversion of organic matter like plants and dead animal remains into carbon** through destructive distillation.
 
• The** gradual process of coal formation from dead vegetation** is known as carbonization.

questions.question: The Northeast Canyons and Seamounts Marine National Monument is located in the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the **__Atlantic Ocean__.**

__
 
• **On September 15, 2016, President Obama designated the first marine national monument in the Atlantic Ocean, the Northeast Canyons and Seamounts Marine National Monument.** 
 
• The **area **has been the subject of **scientific exploration and discovery** since the 1970s.
 
• This is the** first and only national marine monument in the Atlantic Ocean.**
 
• These undersea canyons and seamounts contain:
 
 
• fragile and largely **pristine deep marine ecosystems** and **rich biodiversity.**
 
• **54 species of deep-sea corals.**
 
• **endangered whales and sea turtles**.
 
• other marine mammals and** numerous fish species.​**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

__
 
• A Strait is a naturally formed, narrow, typically navigable waterway that connects two larger bodies of water.

 
 

 
 
 Straits

 
 
 
 Connections

 
 
 

 
 
 Gibraltar Strait 

 
 
 
 It connects the Atlantic Ocean to the Mediterranean sea.

 
 
 

 
 
 Dover Strait

 
 
 
 It connects the boundary between the English Channel and the North Sea 

 
 
 

 
 
 Bering Strait

 
 
 
 It connects the Arctic Ocean with the Pacific ocean

 
 
 

 
 
 Sunda Strait

 
 
 
 It connects the Java sea to the Indian Ocean

 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** ​Atlantic Ocean**

 
 
• ​The **second-largest ocean on Earth.**
 
• The Atlantic drives our weather patterns, including hurricanes. 
 
• It is **home to many species from sea turtles to dolphins.**
 
• The Atlantic Ocean has been** a key avenue of trade and travel.**
 
 
 
• **Arctic Ocean ****​**
 
 
• ​The Arctic Ocean is the **smallest and shallowest of the world's five major oceans.**
 
• It spans an area of **approximately 14,060,000 km².**
 
• It is known as the** coldest of all the oceans.**
 
• The Arctic Ocean is** Earth's northernmost body of water.**
 
 
 
• **Red Sea​**
 
 
• **Saltiest sea of all the seas** that connect to the ocean without even one river that meets the sea.
 
• A popular hypothesis about the origins of the Red Sea's name is that** it contains cyanobacteria called Trichodesmium erythraeum, which turns the normally blue-green water reddish-brown.**
 
• It is the** major spot for scuba diving and snorkeling.**
 
• It has m**ore than 1200 fish species that including 44 sharks, **which makes it the best place to get into marine life.
 
 
 
• **Arabian Sea**
 
 
• ​The Arabian Sea, the northwestern part of the Indian Ocean, **lies between India and the Arabian Peninsula.**
 
• It has** an area of about 1,491,000 sq miles **and an **average depth of 8,970 feet.**
 
• **One of the world's busiest shipping lanes,** primarily due to its proximity to the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf.

questions.question: In which of the following years did the Indian army free Goa from the Portuguese?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1961**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Goa Liberation Day

 
 
• India attained independence from British rule back in 1947, but it would still take Goa, which was a Portuguese colony at the time-14 more years to be liberated from foreign control.
 
• On December 19, 1961, Indian armed personnel managed to wrest control of Goa from the Portuguese, ending around 450 years of colonial rule.
 
• The Goa Opinion Poll was a referendum held in the state of Goa, India on 16 January 1967, to decide the future of the Union Territory of Goa, Daman, and Diu within the Indian Union.
 
• The fight for freedom began in the 1940s as India inched closer to independence from British rule.
 
• The Portuguese colonized several parts of India in 1510 but by the end of the 19th century Portuguese colonies in India were limited to Goa, Daman, Diu, Dadra, Nagar Haveli, and Anjediva Island.
 
• On 30th May 1987, the territory was split and Goa was formed, Daman and Diu remained a Union Territory.​

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India deal with the right to equality?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**14 to 18**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Article 14 to Article 18 of the Constitution of India guarantees the right to equality for every citizen of India. 
 
• This deals with the general principles of equality.
 
• Article 14 of the constitution states that:
 
 
• The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
 
• This article constitutes of 2 parts, being:
 
 
• Equality before law and
 
• Equal protection of the laws
 
 
 
 
 
• Article 15 prohibits discrimination against citizens on such specific grounds as religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
• Article 16 guarantees equality of opportunity in matters of employment under the state. The right is available to citizens only.
 
• Article 17 deals with a peculiar problem in our country. Howsoever praiseworthy the caste system in its origin might have been, it certainly proved to be a disgrace to humanity, a threat to unity, and a serious hindrance to the social, educational, and economic progress of our country. 
 
• Article 18 abolishes titles, other than a military or academic distinction.

• It is focused on the **twin objectives:**
 
 
• constructing toilets.
 
• enabling behavioural change of individuals.
 
 
 
• It focused on the** goal of making India Open Defecation free by 2nd October 2019.​**

questions.solution:

__
 
• **Abul Fazl-i-Allami described in Ain-i-Akbari that during the period of Mughal Emperor Akbar, the gaz was used as the unit of measuring length.**
 
• Each **gaz was divided into 24 equal parts and each part was called Tassuj.**
 
• Gaz was extensively** used to measure land pieces, for the construction of buildings, houses, wells, gardens, and roads.**
 
• The gaz was** widely used as a unit of length till the metric system** was introduced in 1956.
 
• Even **today** in many parts of our country, particularly** in the rural areas, gaz is being used as a unit of length.​**
